title: The nature of the "pseudogap" in the insulating phase of highly disordered superconductors
authors: Mark Nikolaevsky, Abhisek Samanta, Nandini Trivedi, Aviad Frydman
abstract: Disordered thin films undergoing a superconductor-insulator transition provide a controlled setting for studying pseudogap physics in the absence of competing electronic orders. Although theory predicts that local Cooper pairing can survive deep into the insulating phase, direct spectroscopic confirmation has remained experimentally inaccessible because tunneling measurements in highly insulating films require ultra-high-resistance junctions and picoampere current sensitivity. Here we combine ultra-high-resistance planar tunneling spectroscopy on amorphous indium oxide films with quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the attractive Hubbard model to probe the single-particle excitation spectrum deep in the insulating regime. We find striking agreement between experiment and theory: the single-particle gap not only survives across the superconductor-insulator transition, but increases substantially with disorder, reaching values more than twice those observed on the superconducting side. With increasing temperature, the gap fills rather than closes, while coherence peaks are suppressed and spectral weight redistributes to energies far exceeding the gap scale. Our results provide direct quantitative experimental confirmation of the theoretically predicted Cooper-pair insulating state with localized Cooper pairs and establish a unified connection between the pseudogap above $T_c$ and the insulating gap as manifestations of pairing without global phase coherence.
summary: This work investigates the pseudogap physics across the superconductor-insulator transition in disordered superconductors using both advanced tunneling spectroscopy and Quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The key finding is that a robust energy gap persists and grows with disorder deep into the insulating state, indicating localized Cooper pairing without global phase coherence. This establishes a crucial link between the high-temperature pseudogap and the insulating gap.
main_problem: To investigate the nature of the pseudogap in the insulating phase of highly disordered superconductors and establish a unified connection between this gap and the superconducting gap above Tc.
main_result: The single-particle gap survives across the superconductor-insulator transition, increases substantially with disorder, and fills upon increasing temperature rather than closing, confirming a Cooper-pair insulating state.
method: Combining ultra-high-resistance planar tunneling spectroscopy on amorphous indium oxide films with Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the attractive Hubbard model.
model_or_system: The study uses highly disordered thin films undergoing an SIT, modeled by the attractive Hubbard Hamiltonian incorporating random onsite disorder. The system is probed via single-particle excitation spectra.
key_observables: Single-particle excitation spectrum (DOS), energy gap ($\Delta$), temperature dependence of spectral weight, and coherence peak behavior.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($V$), interaction strength ($U/t$), Temperature ($T$), and the proximity to the Superconductor-Insulator Transition (SIT).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting tunneling conductance ($	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$) as a measure of the single-particle density of states, and that QMC simulations accurately capture local pairing physics.
figures_summary: Figures compare DOS measurements showing gap growth with disorder (Fig. 1), demonstrate temperature filling rather than closing of the gap (Fig. 2), and illustrate spectral weight redistribution to high energies (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting experimental difficulty, presents the theoretical framework using the attractive Hubbard model, details the combined experimental/simulation approach, and concludes by showing quantitative agreement confirming a localized Cooper-pair insulating state.
why_interesting: The findings provide direct evidence for pairing mechanisms persisting deep into an insulating regime, which is highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity in correlated materials.

FIG. 4. Schematic illustration of superconductivity in a highly disordered potential in the insulating phase of the superconduc- tor–insulator transition (SIT). The gray surface represents a spatially random disorder potential, with red spheres denoting bound electron pairs localized in potential minima. Purple regions indicate locally coherent superconducting (SC) islands, with arrows representing the local SC phase within each island. At strong disorder, large potential barriers suppress coupling between islands, preventing global phase coherence across the sample.

FIG. 6. Comparison between the effect of parallel vs. perpen- dicular magnetic field on the samples. Zero-bias conductance at H = 0, normalized by its value at field H, for the same sample measured with magnetic field applied parallel (blue) and perpendic- ular (red) to the film. A perpendicular field can introduce vortices, which locally create subgap states and would therefore enhance the zero-bias conductance. Although the low-field responses differ, both orientations converge to essentially the same value at H = 9T. This demonstrates that vortex-induced subgap states cannot account for the observed filling of the gap.
